papers.title: The Virtual Biotech: A multi-agent AI framework for therapeutic discovery and development.
papers.authors: Zhang HG, Eckmann P, Miao J, Mahon AB, Zou J.
papers.abstract: Drug development requires evidence integration across biological scales and modalities, but relevant tools are fragmented. We introduce the Virtual Biotech, an organization of artificial intelligence (AI) agents modeled on a drug-development company, with agentic divisions spanning target discovery, safety assessment, modality selection, and clinical development. We demonstrate its utility at three drug-development decision points. First, more than 37,000 agents annotated outcomes from 55,984 trials and found that drugs targeting cell type-specific genes were 48% more likely to reach market with 32% fewer adverse events. Second, it integrated multimodal evidence to propose a therapeutic strategy in lung cancer. Third, it analyzed a terminated ulcerative colitis trial and inferred potential mechanisms of failure. These results demonstrate that human-guided multi-agent systems can conduct transparent, multiscale analyses to inform therapeutic-development decisions.

papers.title: CauTrigger: deciphering biological system state transitions by hierarchical causal decomposition.
papers.authors: Zhang C, Cai D, Aihara K, Chen L.
papers.abstract: Biological systems exhibit complex hierarchical regulation, with interactions across multiple layers governing transitions between states. Identifying the causal architecture underlying these state transitions remains challenging because confounding can produce spurious associations in observational data. Here we present CauTrigger, a hierarchical deep latent variable model that integrates do-calculus to identify potential causal triggers and predict perturbation outcomes across multiple regulatory layers. By disentangling causal and spurious latent factors, CauTrigger recursively reconstructs the underlying regulatory hierarchy and enables interpretable reasoning from observational data. Across synthetic and real-world datasets with multilayer regulatory structures, CauTrigger outperforms existing methods in identifying causal triggers and forecasting system-level responses. Applied to single-cell multi-omics and gut microbiome datasets, CauTrigger prioritizes candidate causal triggers and uses in silico perturbations to generate testable hypotheses about biological state transitions and inform potential strategies for state navigation. Together, these results establish CauTrigger as a general-purpose framework for causal discovery in complex biological systems.

papers.title: Current-Driven Molecular Machine with Rotation-Enhanced Conductance.
papers.authors: Singh AK, Martin L, Sršen M, Guttesen FS, Hu BZ, Ito Y, Pedersen SK, Kamounah FS, Pauly F, Pittelkow M, Lü JT, Hedegård P, Tal O.
papers.abstract: For more than two millennia, Archimedean screws have been used for water pumping and, more recently, as turbines in hydroelectric power stations[1]. Their helical-blade structure, essential to their function, is also found in chiral molecules and nanostructures, where injected electric current has been proposed to generate torque-mediated rotation[2,3]. Here, we present a torque-driven molecular machine with a rotor actuated by electric current and conductance enhanced by its rotation. Suspending a helicene molecule between two electrode tips, we show that an applied voltage induces cyclic molecular motion with 100% directional preference that can be inverted by the voltage's polarity. Above a voltage threshold, the current through the rotating molecule is significantly enhanced, and the enhancement onset is tuned by stretching or compressing the helical molecule. Such effects were absent in previous helical molecular junctions, likely due to structural and operational differences[4-6]. Calculations show that molecular rotation by current-induced forces explains both the observed cyclic motion and current enhancement. This mechanism predicts a transition from stepwise to continuous rotation at a threshold voltage, yielding a current increase as rotation allows adopting highly conducting configurations not accessible at rest. Our work introduces a prototype for a new class of torque-driven molecular machines with perfect rotor unidirectionality and significant current modulation.

papers.title: Incidence and Risk Factors of Recurrent Visual Field Progression in Glaucoma.
papers.authors: Malek DA, da Costa DR, Scherer R, Medeiros FA.
papers.abstract: Importance A confirmed visual field progression event in glaucoma typically prompts intensification of intraocular pressure (IOP)-lowering therapy, yet the factors associated with recurrent progression after that first event remain poorly characterized. Objective To evaluate the incidence of recurrent visual field progression after an initial Guided Progression Analysis (GPA) likely-progression event and the factors associated with a recurrent event. Design, setting, and participants This cohort study was conducted among patients receiving routine ophthalmic care between 1998 and 2025 at a single tertiary academic center (Bascom Palmer Ophthalmic Registry). Data were analyzed from February 2026 to August 2026. Main outcomes and measures The primary outcomes were the cumulative probability of recurrent visual field progression and hazard ratios (HRs) for factors associated with recurrence. Results A total of 7457 eyes of 5086 patients with open-angle glaucoma or suspected glaucoma were included, with a mean (SD) follow-up of 12.4 (4.6) years. Mean (SD) patient age was 60.5 (13.1) years, and 4468 eyes (59.9%) were from female patients. By self-reported race and ethnicity, 203 eyes (2.7%) were from Asian patients, 1718 (23.0%) from Black patients, 1677 (22.5%) from Hispanic patients, and 5536 (74.2%) from White patients. A total of 1951 eyes (26.2%) developed initial GPA likely progression; 635 eyes had adequate follow-up after first progression and IOP data. Among those, 167 (26.3%) recurred. Kaplan-Meier cumulative recurrence was 13.8% at 3 years (95% CI, 11.6%-17.1%) and 43.5% at 10 years (95% CI, 35.8%-52.1%). In multivariable Cox analysis, faster mean deviation (MD) loss before first progression (HR, 1.73 per 1 decibel [dB]/y; 95% CI, 1.39-2.15), higher mean IOP after the first event (HR, 1.09 per 1 mm Hg; 95% CI, 1.05-1.13), less negative MD at first progression (HR, 1.08 per 1 dB; 95% CI, 1.04-1.12), and older age (HR, 1.11 per 5 years; 95% CI, 1.03-1.19) were independently associated with recurrence. Each 10% greater IOP reduction was associated with lower hazard (HR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.83-0.94). Among eyes with pre-event MD slopes faster than -1.0 dB/y, recurrence occurred in 42.7% of eyes vs 23.4% in slower-progressing eyes (difference, 19.3%; 95% CI, 8.8%-29.9%). Conclusions and relevance Findings from this cohort study suggest that recurrent visual field progression after a first GPA progression event is common; eyes at highest risk had faster pre-event visual field loss, less advanced damage at first progression, higher postevent IOP, and older age. These results may help target intensified monitoring and IOP lowering toward higher-risk eyes.

papers.title: Resident to Urgent Eye Clinic Transformation and Association With Health Equity and Resident Education.
papers.authors: Ojo S, Dogra N, Wallace L, DiLoreto DA, Wozniak RAF, Hu WF.
papers.abstract: Importance US ophthalmology residency programs are divided between traditional resident clinic-based models with a separate faculty practice, and universal practice-based models. Little data exist comparing these educational models. Objective To evaluate the association of changing a traditional resident clinic training model to a universal practice plus urgent eye clinic-based residency training model with sociodemographic disparities and resident education. Design, setting, and participants This was a cross-sectional study conducted at a US academic medical center. All patients presenting to the University of Rochester Flaum Eye Institute between the period July 1, 2017, to June 30, 2019, and the period July 1, 2022, to June 30, 2024, were divided into 4 cohorts for retrospective analysis as follows: resident clinic 2017-2019, faculty practice 2017-2019, urgent eye clinic 2022-2024, and universal practice 2022-2024. Exposures The resident clinic was transitioned to urgent eye clinic in July 2022. All former patients from resident clinic were reassigned to the new universal practice. Main outcomes and measures Patient cohorts were compared regarding insurance payor(s) and self-identified race. Level of disease acuity in resident clinic and urgent eye clinic were compared. Graduating resident procedural volumes were compared. Results Participants were divided into the following 4 cohorts: resident clinic 2017-2019 (6819 patients), faculty practice 2017-2019 (61 847 patients), urgent eye clinic 2022-2024 (5124 patients), and universal practice 2022-2024 (79 001 patients), for a total of 118 459 patients (mean [SD] age, 47 [25] years; 65 186 female [55%]). Pretransition, compared with faculty practice patients, greater proportions of resident clinic patients used Medicaid insurance (62.1% vs 19.4%; difference, 32.0%; 95% CI, 30.9%-33.1%; P Conclusions and relevance Results of this cross-sectionals study show that transforming resident clinic into urgent eye clinic was associated with reduced sociodemographic disparities, enhanced resident exposure to high-acuity disease, and increased resident procedural experience. These results suggest that changes in resident clinic structure may improve both health equity and resident education.

papers.title: Lifestyle-induced regulatory T cell fragility primes adverse events after immune checkpoint blockade.
papers.authors: Patra D, Wolfgang K, Ye C, Rigatti L, Ertwine K, Morder KM, Jana J, Baral I, Hurd D, Bossong K, Mullett S, Dou Y, Gelhaus S, Vignali DAA, Davar D, Cillo AR, Delgoffe GM, Overacre-Delgoffe AE.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade has transformed cancer therapy, but immune-related adverse events (irAEs) remain a major, sometimes fatal, limitation, and the lack of robust preclinical models has hindered mechanistic insight. We present the lifestyle-induced susceptibility to irAEs (LISA) model, in which diet-driven metabolic and microbial alterations recreate human-like susceptibility to anti-PD-1 toxicity. LISA recapitulates multi-organ irAEs with immune infiltration and cytokine production, severity depending on sex, age, treatment modality, and immunotherapy response. Mechanistically, dysbiosis marked by Akkermansia muciniphila enrichment accompanies aberrant immune activation, driving regulatory T cell (Treg) fragility and CD8 + cytotoxic effector populations, both observed in patients with irColitis. Dietary reversal, metabolite supplementation, and blocking interferon (IFN)-γ production or signaling in Tregs restored Treg stability and resolved inflammation. Human-to-mouse fecal microbiome transfer interacts with recipient diet to shape susceptibility. Together, these findings identify dietary, microbial, and immune drivers of irAEs, which can be leveraged to improve immunotherapy responses while minimizing toxicity.

papers.title: MCT6 is an intestinal Lac-Phe exporter required for metformin-associated weight loss.
papers.authors: Xiao S, Tung AS, Spaas J, Fu S, Chen X, Trinh TK, Moya-Garzon MD, Li VL, Cessna HT, Ito K, Reghupaty SC, Lin C, Lyu X, Raun SH, Tyner MDW, Germakovski A, Tondreau J, Yeckley M, Wei W, Howitt MR, Parker MD, Sprowl JA, Hinshaw SM, Long JZ.
papers.abstract: Metabolites are increasingly recognized as circulating molecules that regulate physiology, yet the mechanisms that couple local intracellular production to organism-wide action remain poorly defined. Using the anorexigenic metabolite N-lactoyl-phenylalanine (Lac-Phe) as a model system, we identify the orphan transporter MCT6/SLC16A5 as a physiologic intestinal Lac-Phe exporter. This mechanism controls the extent to which intracellularly synthesized Lac-Phe acquires systemic activity. MCT6 transports Lac-Phe in vitro, mediates Lac-Phe efflux in cells, and is required for maintaining normal circulating Lac-Phe levels in vivo, particularly following metformin treatment or high-intensity exercise. High-fat-diet-fed mice with global or intestinal epithelial-specific deletion of MCT6 exhibit resistance to metformin-associated weight loss. Bypassing the transport defect with exogenous Lac-Phe normalizes the body weight phenotype of MCT6-knockout (KO) mice. These data connect MCT6 to Lac-Phe and gut glycolytic flux and underscore the importance of transporter-mediated release in the conversion of an intracellular metabolic state into a circulating metabolite effector.

papers.title: Metazoan lagging-strand DNA synthesis is distributive.
papers.authors: Lynch LD, Park J, Chistol G.
papers.abstract: DNA's anti-parallel structure presents a topological challenge to the replisome, as leading and lagging strands must be synthesized in opposite directions. How lagging-strand synthesis is coordinated with leading-strand synthesis remains unresolved in eukaryotes. To address this question, we directly visualized the dynamics of lagging-strand polymerases Pol α and Pol δ at active replication forks using single-molecule imaging in Xenopus nuclear extracts. Surprisingly, we find that neither Pol α nor Pol δ is stably tethered to the replisome. Instead, lagging-strand synthesis occurs distributively and entails the rapid recruitment of new molecules of Pol α and Pol δ for each Okazaki fragment. Consequently, leading- and lagging-strand synthesis are not intrinsically coupled. We propose that metazoans solve the problem of anti-parallel replication not by actively coordinating leading- and lagging-strand synthesis, but instead simply by recruiting new polymerases to synthesize each Okazaki fragment.

papers.title: Association Between Systemic TNF-α Inhibitor Use and Risk of Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma.
papers.authors: Hong AT, Lin F, Xu BY, Weinreb RN.
papers.abstract: Purpose To evaluate the association between systemic tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) inhibitor use and the long-term risk of primary open angle glaucoma (POAG), and to compare glaucoma risk among users of different TNF-α inhibitors. Design Retrospective, multicenter clinical cohort study. Methods This retrospective, multicenter cohort study compared patients ≥40 years with and without TNF-α inhibitor use (2006-2026) using data from aggregated, de-identified electronic health records across 70 U.S. health care organizations. Patients prescribed TNF-α inhibitors (adalimumab, infliximab, etanercept, certolizumab pegol, or golimumab) were propensity matched (1:1) to controls without TNF-α inhibitor exposure based on demographics and systemic indications for TNF-a. Patients with a history of uveitis and related sequelae were excluded. New POAG diagnosis, identified by ICD-10 codes within 10 years of follow-up, was assessed using Cox proportional hazards models. Results Among 12,227 TNF-α inhibitor users and 1,354,651 controls, 11,915 matched pairs were analyzed (mean [SD] age 59 [10] years; 68% female). At 10 years, TNF-α inhibitor users were associated with a lower risk of POAG diagnosis compared to controls (2.0% vs. 3.3%; HR 0.70 [95% CI 0.59-0.82]; P Conclusions Systemic TNF-α inhibitor use, particularly adalimumab and infliximab, was associated with a modest but significant reduction in long-term POAG risk. These findings support a potential role of TNF-α-mediated inflammation in glaucomatous neurodegeneration.

papers.title: The mRNA-based RSV vaccine mRNA-1345 induces robust and durable CD4 + T cell responses against RSV in younger and older adults.
papers.authors: DiPiazza A, Marcisak E, Yu WH, Makrinos D, Kuo HH, Landy J, McGrath S, Chang X, Cavallaro M, Wu C, Essene A, Lin H, Walker L, Carfi A, Oostendorp J, Paris R, Sun Y.
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a health threat, particularly for infants, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals. Although neutralizing antibodies can help limit infection and viral replication, T cells are essential for reducing disease severity. Assessment of age-related declines in T cell function are important for vaccine evaluation. We used intracellular cytokine staining, activation-induced marker, and Meso Scale Discovery assays and single-cell multiomic profiling to evaluate RSV vaccine mRNA-1345 responses in younger and older adults. mRNA-1345 induced comparable CD4 + and CD8 + T cell responses in both cohorts, with CD4 + responses persisting for 24 months. The CD4 + response was strongly T helper 1 (T H 1)-polarized, with increased interferon-γ, interleukin-2, and tumor necrosis factor-α and minimal T H 2 cytokines. Both CD4 + and CD8 + T cells showed increased polyfunctionality that remained elevated at 2 years. Single-cell and T cell receptor repertoire analyses showed similar Pre-F-specific phenotypes, transcriptional profiles, and clonal overlap across age groups, supporting robust, durable cellular immunity after mRNA-1345 vaccination. These findings indicate shared vaccine-elicited T cell immunity in adults.

papers.title: Single-cell-level digital twins for preterm birth prevention strategies.
papers.authors: Einhaus J, Neidlinger P, Fondeur O, Sato M, Anronikov S, Miyazaki K, Maechler A, Amar JN, Ando K, Badea V, Gaudilliere DK, Sabayev M, Feyaerts D, Diop M, Tsai AS, Cambriel A, Ganio EA, Lagarde R, O'Kelly E, Stelzer IA, Hedou J, Wong RJ, Blumenfeld YJ, Lyell DJ, Shaw GM, Oskotsky TT, Sirota M, Giudice LC, Stevenson DK, Aghaeepour N, Gaudilliere B.
papers.abstract: Digital twin models can accelerate therapeutic development by enabling low-risk testing of candidate interventions. In preterm labor (PTL), a major pregnancy complication where clinical trials face ethical and financial barriers, digital twins are especially valuable for evaluating new therapies targeting immune dysfunctions driving PTL. Yet, current models lack single-cell resolution, limiting detection of cell type-specific mechanisms, off-target effects, and the design of personalized interventions. We present Simulated Immunome Modeling of Clinical Outcomes (SIMCO), a single-cell-level digital twin framework that models immunomodulatory treatment effects on the timing of labor using immunome-wide, single-cell simulations. SIMCO's digital twins are trained and validated on a newly generated mass cytometry atlas of the pregnant immunome exposed to nine candidate drugs preselected for PTL prevention. Applying SIMCO to an independent cohort of pregnant individuals, we simulate treatment effects on gestational length, screening for candidate drugs that delay labor timing and providing system-level mechanistic insight for each drug candidate. Tetrahydrofolate and the combination of aspirin and lansoprazole emerged as top candidates for PTL prevention, delaying labor onset primarily through enhanced mTOR signaling in innate immune cells and attenuated JAK/STAT signaling in naïve CD4 + T cells.

papers.title: OCT to Assess Risk of Progression of Multiple Sclerosis: A Report by the American Academy of Ophthalmology.
papers.authors: Moss HE, Oke I, Chen JJ, Dinkin MJ, El-Dairi MA, Gaier ED, Gilbert AL, MacIntosh PW, Pineles SL, Heidary G.
papers.abstract: Purpose To review the current published literature on the utility of OCT of the retina in peripapillary and macular regions to predict or assess risk of disease activity in adult patients with multiple sclerosis (MS) and MS precursors (radiologically isolated syndrome and clinically isolated syndrome). Methods A literature search of the PubMed database was last performed in September 2025. Articles were limited to original research in the English language that included adult patients. The search yielded 275 articles that were examined in abstract form to exclude reviews, and 71 were reviewed in full text. Twenty-one articles were selected for inclusion in this assessment and were assigned a level of evidence rating by the panel methodologist. Results Two studies were rated level I, 8 studies were rated level II, and 11 studies were rated level III. Baseline measurements (lower thickness, faster thickness decline, and larger interocular thickness differences) of the peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer (pRNFL) and macular ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer (GC-IPL) from OCT scans in patients with MS and precursors of MS were associated with future progression of MS as measured by disability, clinical relapses, and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) changes. Multiple variable models support the independent association of OCT metrics and MS progression. Conclusions Evidence supports the development of OCT-derived pRNFL and macular GC-IPL thickness measurements as biomarkers for future progression of MS in patients with MS or MS precursor syndromes. Future work is needed to improve generalizability by studying demographically heterogeneous cohorts and should include determining the comparability of metrics obtained from different OCT manufacturers' hardware and software. Future research is also needed to guide interpretation of OCT in the context of other predictors of future disease activity such as MRI. papers.title: Recordanelles for transcriptome-wide single-cell RNA recording in human cells.
papers.authors: Reinkemeier CD, Manero-Carranza M, Farouni R, Filice F, Klotz A, Schneider-Heieck K, Andermann TL, Platt RJ.
papers.abstract: Transcriptomic measurement technologies provide powerful approaches to understand biology but are limited to providing either a high-resolution snapshot at a moment in time or a low-resolution history of transcription constrained to a few genes over a narrow time range. Here, we introduce the 'recordanelle', a single-component synthetic organelle capable of recording the transcriptome in human cells. Recordanelles are composed of a mitochondrial membrane anchor, a condensate assembler and a poly(A)-binding protein. We demonstrate that the recordanelle can be engineered to recruit engineered RNAs or a sampling of up to 90% of all endogenous mRNAs and protect them over several days. We further show that transient and dynamic transcriptional responses resulting from inducible promoters or interferon signaling are preserved throughout time within the recordanelle at the single-cell level. This work provides a nondisruptive and unbiased transcriptome-wide single-cell RNA recording technology to enable a deeper understanding of biology.

papers.title: Deep dynamical models of single-cell multiomic velocities predict loss-of-function and rescue perturbations in B cells.
papers.authors: Karbalayghareh A, Pelzer B, Chin CR, Melnick A, Barisic D, Leslie CS.
papers.abstract: Here we present DynaVelo, a generative neural ordinary differential equation model that learns the joint dynamics of gene expression and transcription factor (TF) motif activity from single-cell multiome data. DynaVelo learns a functional form of the vector field, such that the model can be perturbed in silico and not only used to draw trajectories. We show that DynaVelo recovers the bifurcating in vivo dynamics of wild-type murine germinal center (GC) B cells and reveals how these dynamics change under heterozygous loss of epigenetic regulators Arid1a and Ctcf. In silico perturbation yields dynamic and cell-state-specific gene regulatory networks (GRNs) that recover known TF-to-gene edges in the wild-type GC GRN and predicts those that are disrupted in mutants. Perturbing Arid1aHet GCs in silico identified Ctcf, Stat3 and Bcl6 as rescue targets for Arid1a loss. In vivo experiments in double-heterozygous mice confirmed rescue of the Arid1aHet dark-zone phenotype in all three cases, and multiome profiling of Arid1aHet;CtcfHet GCs validated the predicted shift toward wild-type dynamics.

papers.title: Additive manufacturing of ultralong and architected single crystals.
papers.authors: Liu C, Cui Y, Wang J, Han X, Ji Z, Liang Z, Zhang C, Marian J, Li Z, Lu T, Xu T, Zhang J, Cui W, Liu W, Fang D, Wang YM.
papers.abstract: Single-crystal materials are indispensable for high-performance applications, yet their deployment remains constrained by conventional manufacturing techniques that depend on strict quasi-steady thermal conditions 1 . This requirement fundamentally conflicts with the intense cyclic thermal fluctuations inherent to additive manufacturing 2 , historically preventing the 3D printing of large or architected single crystals. Here we present a free-form additive manufacturing approach that resolves this contradiction by using delicately controlled alternating and pulsed heat inputs to govern and direct single-crystal growth. Using this method, we demonstrate the fabrication of metre-tall, centimetre-diameter single-crystal Ti-6Al-4V alongside, to our knowledge, the first single-crystal lattice structures containing complex zigzag ligaments, effectively eliminating theoretical size constraints for single-crystal components. The resulting bulk single-crystal Ti-6Al-4V exhibits an order-of-magnitude increase in creep resistance over standard grain-size scaling predictions, driven by the synergistic elimination of grain boundaries and an additive manufacturing-induced hierarchical α/β-architecture that regulates dislocation density, mobility and void evolution. Furthermore, we demonstrate the broad applicability of this technique by printing single crystals of hard-to-process refractory metals, including W, Mo, Nb and MoNb alloys. Our work introduces a large-scale method for single-crystal additive manufacturing, expanding the accessible materials library and enabling high-performance, complex geometries previously unattainable by classical methods.

papers.title: Zeolite-catalysed olefin carbonylation based on tuning spatial confinement.
papers.authors: Qi L, Sheng Y, Zhang W, Ni Y, He L, Li B, Wang A, Zhu W, Bell AT, Liu Z.
papers.abstract: Carbonylation is an important process used to produce aldehydes, carboxylic acids and esters 1-5 that is usually catalysed by homogeneous metal complexes with ligands and iodide promoters 6-12 . Koch has reported that protons of mineral acids can also catalyse carbonylation 13 . Previous studies have demonstrated that Brønsted acidic zeolites can act as a heterogeneous, Koch-type catalyst for carbonylation of alcohols and olefins, but the products in this case are limited to tertiary carboxylic acids 14-18 . Here we show that targeted use of spatial confinement in a zeolite together with a high CO/olefin ratio can help break this limitation. We report that, with FER zeolite and a CO/olefin ratio of 360, olefin carbonylation can produce primary and secondary carboxylic acids as the main products; ethylene carbonylation to propanoic acid (PA) is achieved with 80% selectivity over 100 h and propylene carbonylation to isobutyric acid (IBA) is achieved with 95% selectivity over 750 h. The propylene and ethylene carbonylation selectivities decrease to 61% and 57%, respectively, as the CO/olefin ratio decreases to 24 and 90, respectively. Experiments in combination with theoretical calculations suggest that T2-O5 in eight-membered ring (8-MR) cavities of FER zeolite are the primary active sites for ethylene carbonylation and T3-O1 in ten-membered rings (10-MRs) are the primary active sites for propylene carbonylation. Our findings open new directions for olefin carbonylation and provide critical insights into the prerequisites for developing new zeolite-based carbonylation processes.

papers.title: An environmentally regulated dichotomy in cell lineages of the root.
papers.authors: Oliva M, Stuart T, Tang D, Khan A, Clement O, Makosa D, Poppe D, Pflueger J, Jabbari JS, Gigante S, Dragwidge JM, Petterson M, Whelan J, Lewsey MG, Lister R.
papers.abstract: Plant development is highly plastic, with growth and architecture continuously shaped by environmental conditions. Roots, for instance, adjust their development to local water, nutrient and soil conditions. Despite this plasticity, individual root cell types are generally viewed as largely homogeneous populations that progress along a single developmental trajectory 1 . Here we show that rather than progressing along a single developmental trajectory, most Arabidopsis root cell lineage trajectories exhibit a stereotyped bifid topology, as revealed by single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcript mapping. One branch is characterized by a transcriptional program that is shared across multiple cell types and enriched for genes associated with environmental responses, including abscisic acid (ABA) signalling. This state occurs reproducibly in a subset of cells across multiple cell types, independent of developmental lineage, thereby revealing an additional layer of root cell identity. It is conserved across Arabidopsis ecotypes and persists despite major perturbations in developmental identity. Moreover, it is reduced in ABA-deficient and ABA-insensitive mutants and becomes more prevalent under water-deficit conditions. Together, these findings reveal an additional layer of root cell identity that is superimposed on developmental lineage and its prevalence is modulated by environmental conditions. These results uncover a previously unrecognized source of environment-associated transcriptional heterogeneity shared across root cell types.

papers.title: Enzyme-embedded polyesters for accelerated biodegradation in the deep sea.
papers.authors: Huang Q, Iida N, Isobe N, Kabe T, Omura T, Ilangovan M, Kimura S, Seok JH, Nomaki H, Kasuya KI, Iwata T.
papers.abstract: The accumulation of persistent plastics in the ocean is causing wide-ranging environmental problems 1-3 . Some commercially available compostable plastics 4-7 , developed to address these issues, degrade efficiently under industrial composting conditions; however, their degradation in marine environments, particularly in the deep sea, remains limited 8-10 . Here we demonstrate that thermally embedding enzymes into compostable polyesters (poly(butylene succinate) (PBS), poly(butylene succinate-co-adipate) (PBSA), poly(ε-caprolactone) (PCL) and poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PBAT)) significantly accelerates their degradation in both coastal and deep-sea environments from water depths of 2-6 m to 5,503 m. Enzyme-embedded polyesters achieved near-complete degradation at a deep-sea depth of 757 m within 5 months. Furthermore, moderate biodegradation of enzyme-embedded polyesters was observed under extreme conditions on deep-sea floors of 5,503 m. In coastal seawater, films embedded with trace amounts (0.1 wt%) of enzyme underwent rapid degradation. The mechanical properties of enzyme-embedded polyesters were similar to those of enzyme-free polyesters. Chemical analysis confirmed the formation of low-molecular-mass degradation products and biochemical oxygen demand measurements supported the mineralization of the enzyme-embedded polyesters. The enzyme-embedding strategy enables enhanced marine degradation of compostable polyesters and represents a potential solution to marine plastic pollution.

papers.title: Persistent neuronal stress signalling underlies Angelman syndrome phenotypes.
papers.authors: Kim KS, Gardner C, Cullen A, Stelzer JA, Cho K, Sharma A, Nemera MT, Law T, Naz H, Zhao G, Gabel HW, Patti GJ, Musiek ES, Ahn TH, Yi JJ.
papers.abstract: Angelman syndrome is a severe neurodevelopmental disorder caused by the loss of UBE3A, a gene that encodes an E3 ubiquitin ligase 1,2 . The mechanisms that underlie Angelman syndrome are not well understood, and in particular, the link between UBE3A substrates and disease phenotypes remains uncertain 3 . Here, using gain- and loss-of-function mutations in UBE3A 4,5 along with unbiased proteomics, we show that asparagine synthetase (ASNS) is a target of UBE3A. We find that ASNS protein abundance is increased in the brains of Ube3a-null mice and in human neurons 6 . Genetic correction of ASNS overabundance rescues microcephaly and many behavioural deficits. Detailed molecular analyses show that ASNS overabundance activates stress signalling and causes a global reduction in neuronal protein synthesis. Our results suggest that loss of UBE3A traps neurons in a state of persistent stress and stunts neuronal growth during developmentally sensitive periods. Moreover, our results indicate that targeting ASNS and the stress response could hold therapeutic potential in Angelman syndrome.

papers.title: De novo design of enantioselective artificial metalloenzyme photocatalysts.
papers.authors: Mishra S, Payal, Evans D, Bortey K, Bootwala H, Gonzalez-Gutierrez G, Vázquez RJ, Baker D, Lewis JC.
papers.abstract: The ability to create protein scaffolds that impart enantioselectivity to simple, readily available metal catalysts could redefine the landscape of asymmetric catalysis. Artificial metalloenzymes (ArMs), hybrid catalysts that combine a synthetic metal cofactor with a protein scaffold, offer a potential means to achieve this goal, but scaffold discovery has remained constrained by trial-and-error approaches and the functional limits of extant proteins. 1-5 This challenge is acute for metal polypyridine photocatalysts, which are widely used in visible-light chemistry but have not enabled highly enantioselective photocatalysis within protein scaffolds. In this study, we show that generative protein design 6-8 can create de novo scaffolds that selectively bind these photocatalysts and that directed evolution converts the resulting artificial metalloenzymes into efficient, highly enantioselective photocatalysts 9 . The evolved proteins support diverse light-driven reactions, high catalyst turnover and catalyst recycling, and can function with commercially available racemic metal complexes. Spectroscopic studies show that the protein environment extends the photocatalyst excited-state lifetime and organizes substrate near the cofactor, altering energy transfer and controlling stereoselectivity. These findings establish de novo protein design as a route to functional scaffolds for synthetic metal complexes that lack natural protein partners and provide a strategy for combining protein design and evolution to control non-natural catalytic chemistry.

papers.title: Drought and disease trigger novel interactions among top predators.
papers.authors: Sergio F, Natsukawa H, Tanferna A, Chicano J, Carro F, Soriguer RC, Hiraldo F, Blas J.
papers.abstract: Interactions among species are increasingly recognized as key determinants of climate change impacts on ecosystems 1-5 . However, we know little about how climatic perturbations affect interactions among top vertebrate predators. Here we show that, when an emergent disease caused the decline of shared prey (rabbits), after decades of neutral co-existence a mammalian carnivore (lynx) started to prey heavily on a top predatory raptor (kites). These predation bouts occurred exclusively under drought conditions and when lynx found rabbit remains under the raptor nests, consistent with the removal of a potential competitor. Drought-induced lynx predation depressed lifetime reproductive success and triggered territory abandonment and dispersal by the raptor, suggestive of a new arms race among predators. A reduction in raptor abundance was associated with an increase in an insectivorous bird (a small owl), showing that the new interaction had the potential to reach lower trophic levels. These results underline the importance of diet flexibility and mobility as important mediators of resilience to stressors. In the future, synergistic effects of multiple anthropogenic stressors may reshape the interactions and ecological roles of many apex predators, with potential cascading consequences for whole ecosystems. A key to forecasting the future impact of global change may reside in understanding how behavioural flexibility and interacting keystone species respond to interacting shocks.

papers.title: A single archaeon couples long-chain fatty acid oxidation to methanogenesis.
papers.authors: Yi Y, Cao Z, Wu K, Ding H, Fu L, Gao W, Li L, Zhou L, Zhou Z, Dai L, Lu Y, Cheng L.
papers.abstract: Anaerobic degradation of complex organic compounds to methane and carbon dioxide is common in the deep subsurface biosphere and has long been considered to require syntrophic cooperation, with methanogens confined to the terminal use of simple C 1 and C 2 substrates. Thermodynamic considerations, multi-omics analyses and microcosm experiments suggest that archaeal lineages are capable of methanogenic degradation of complex substrates 1-6 . However, experimental validation in pure culture was lacking. Here we report the isolation of a thermophilic archaeon, Methanoglobus dolicholipophagus AA-75, affiliated with Archaeoglobi, from a Chinese petroleum reservoir. Strain AA-75 not only converts methanol into methane, carbon dioxide and acetate, but also uses saturated fatty acids varying from C7:0 to C18:0 and unsaturated fatty acids including C16:1, C18:1 and C18:2 to produce methane. We term the latter lipotrophic methanogenesis, which integrates β-oxidation of fatty acids with the Wood-Ljungdahl pathway and the canonical methyl-tetrahydromethanopterin:coenzyme M methyltransferase and methyl-coenzyme M reductase complexes, together with an intracellular electron transfer system. A formaldehyde-methanol branch probably functions as an auxiliary route for C 1 metabolism during methanogenesis. Methane produced from stearate is moderately 13 C-enriched (δ 13 C-CH 4 = -40.0‰ to -36.3‰), distinct from the strong 13 C depletion characteristic of canonical methanogenic pathways. These findings demonstrate that methanogens can function as primary degraders of complex organic matter, challenging the classical syntrophic paradigm and calling for refinement of current models of carbon cycling in the deep subsurface biosphere.

papers.title: GRP75-dependent SIMPA mediates inter-organellar quality control.
papers.authors: Yu F, Jiang L, Liu H, Yang S, Yuan Y, Jin H, Liu J, Liu X, Dong Y, Ren D, Kang J, Huang Y, Meng Q, Bai F, Li Y, Li S, Liu H, Zhao W, Xiao J, Chen Q.
papers.abstract: Mitochondria are bound by a double membrane and are semiautonomous organelles, rendering them highly vulnerable to global and internal proteostatic stress 1 . Multiple surveillance mechanisms at proteostatic and inter-organellar levels have evolved to maintain mitochondrial integrity and cellular health 2-7 . However, the precise mechanisms by which proteostatic damage relays stress signals across organelles and how the quality surveillance machinery coordinates these functions remain unknown. Here we report that under proteostatic stress, damaged mitochondrial proteins are sequestered to form stress-induced mitochondrial protein aggregates (SIMPAs) that activate specific quality control mechanisms in a spatially confined manner without perturbing the mitochondrial network. Quantitative proteomic and correlative light-electron microscopy analysis revealed that SIMPA mediates inter-organellar communication via mitochondria-endoplasmic reticulum contact sites or mitochondrial-associated membranes. Mechanistically, GRP75 coordinates SIMPA biogenesis and focally activates endoplasmic reticulum unfolded protein response pathways via mitochondria-endoplasmic reticulum contact sites or mitochondrial-associated membranes for the targeted clearance of SIMPAs. Functionally, in both cellular and liver disease models, we found that a GRP75-dependent SIMPA signalling cascade attenuates mitochondrial stress and preserves mitochondrial integrity under proteotoxic stress. Overall, we show that SIMPAs, functioning as protein condensates, serve as a central cross-compartment communication hub for mitochondrial quality control, supporting cellular and organismal fitness.

papers.title: Functional architecture of the human insula.
papers.authors: Quabs J, Pantis S, Chen G, Huang W, Ma E, Del Vecchio M, Lyu D, Wang C, Avanzini P, Buch V, Ramayya AG, Caspers S, Vogel H, Parvizi J.
papers.abstract: The insular cortex has a central role in pain 1,2 , interoception 3,4 and feelings 5,6 , yet its functional architecture and causal electrophysiological relationships among its subregions remain poorly understood. Here we combine intracranial electrical stimulation and task-based electroencephalography recordings with connectivity mapping within a cytoarchitectonic atlas of the human insula 7-10 in 87 participants implanted with intracranial electrodes, and identify a quadripartite functional architecture comprising four distinct regions: (1) a dorsal-posterior region encoding somatotopically organized nociceptive/thermoceptive and somatosensory signals; (2) a ventral-posterior region with access to somatic information across multiple body parts; (3) a mid-anterior region associated with visceral sensations and anxiety states; and (4) an anterior-polar region, largely silent to direct stimulation, yet showing robust activation during salience detection and change of action mode. Critically, this anterior region, with its strong connections with the prefrontal cortex, including the anterior cingulate cortex, exerts strong and direct influence over other insular regions, while receiving less-strong indirect inputs from them, revealing an electrophysiological pathway for cognitive modulation of pain and bodily perception. Together, these findings define a functional architecture of the human insula that links cytoarchitecture to directed and asymmetric electrophysiological interactions, with mechanistic implications for cognitive modulation of pain and interoceptive experience.

papers.title: Programmable design of functional proteins from natural language.
papers.authors: Dai F, You S, Zhu Y, Gao Y, Fu L, Zhou X, Su J, Wang C, Fan Y, Tan Q, Ma X, Deng X, Yu L, Qian H, He Y, Ke Y, Zhang Z, Han C, Chang X, Zheng L, Wang S, Ji Y, Hao K, Cao L, Wang Y, Zeng A, Wang S, Zhan C, Zhao J, Si T, Liu J, Lu H, Yuan F.
papers.abstract: Programming biological function-designing bespoke proteins to perform specified molecular tasks-is a foundational goal of molecular engineering. However, current design models remain fundamentally limited 1-3 : they typically require either natural proteins as starting points for optimization or manual reformulation of functional goals as geometric and sequence-level constraints to guide candidate generation. Here we introduce Pinal, a 16-billion-parameter foundation model that designs candidate proteins from natural-language descriptions of desired function. Trained on 1.7 billion synthetically annotated protein-text pairs, Pinal links functional intent to protein sequence and structure. In computational evaluations, generated candidates combined high predicted foldability with functional-description alignment and sequence diversity, providing a basis for prioritizing experimentally testable designs. We applied Pinal to four distinct design tasks-a fluorescent protein, a polyethylene terephthalate hydrolase, an alcohol dehydrogenase and a metabolic H-protein-and experimentally observed the intended function in each case, including catalytic activity for both designed enzymes. Without iterative experimental optimization, a Pinal-designed H-protein increased product titre by 1.7-fold relative to the corresponding native Escherichia coli H-protein in a multi-enzyme CO 2 fixation pathway. These findings support natural language as a high-level interface for candidate generation in protein design, enabling programmable exploration with reduced reliance on manually specified structural or sequence constraints.

papers.title: Contrasting demographic impacts of Roman colonization and early medieval migrations in the Iberian Peninsula.
papers.authors: Carrión P, Olalde I, McCormick M, Harper K, Garcia-Collado MI, Villalba-Mouco V, Jiménez-Arenas JM, Coromina N, Vivó D, Vergès JM, Costa A, Botella Ortega D, Bustamante-Álvarez M, Heras-Mora J, Ortega-Ruiz R, Chaves C, Quirós-Castillo JA, Roig J, Suárez-Padilla J, Navarro-Luengo I, Cuadrado-Prieto MÁ, Aguilera I, Morera J, Catalán R, Cerdeño ML, Roig-Pérez JF, Díaz-García M, Chirosa-Cañavate P, Piza-Ruiz T, Vallejo-Casas E, Vidal-Álvarez S, Burch J, Sagrera J, Vivo J, Cubo-Córdoba A, Martínez-Enamorado V, Rengel-Castro F, García-Entero V, Rodero A, Viguera E, Rohland N, Morales JI, Soto M, Mallick S, Cebrià A, García-Borja P, Bardoll PC, Ulloa-Eres P, Carretero-Pérez A, Gómez-Espinosa T, Campderá Gutiérrez B, Pagés-Alonso P, Vara-Izquierdo C, Martínez-Peñarroya J, Sardà-Seuma S, Castaño-Aguilar JM, López-Chamizo S, Pinhasi R, Lalueza-Fox C, Reich D.
papers.abstract: It has been unclear how Roman and later Germanic political control shaped the demography of Iberia and how it differed from other parts of Europe. We report genetic data from 243 ancient individuals dating to 100-800 CE, analyzed alongside 58 previously published individuals. In Roman times, we document an influx of people with ancestry from the Eastern Mediterranean and an influx of North Africans, especially in the center and south. Beginning in the 5th century, Germanic and Alan (Sarmatian) groups assumed political control. Although we identify individuals with Central-Northern European-associated ancestry, including siblings buried ∼725 km apart, the Hispano-Roman population remained continuous in Iberia. These demographic patterns contrast sharply with those in Britain, where major demographic change followed Rome's collapse, and with those in the central Mediterranean, where both periods were associated with profound transformations. Together, these findings highlight regional variation in admixture and continuity across post-Roman Europe.

papers.title: Proteomic atlas of T cell exhaustion defines proteostatic collapse.
papers.authors: Shuttleworth SL, Bauer MA, Province DW, Kelliher JL, Scharping NE, Monell A, Rogers LJ, Williams TA, Dawson GT, Wallis KF, Alkam D, Edmondson JL, Fil D, Storey AJ, Bolding AL, Edmondson RD, Byrum SD, Beenken KE, Mackintosh SG, Goldrath AW, Tackett AJ, Koss B.
papers.abstract: T cell exhaustion limits the success of cancer immunotherapies, yet the proteomic changes underlying this dysfunctional state remain poorly understood. We integrated transcriptomics, quantitative proteomics, turnover proteomics, and ubiquitin proteomics to construct a multi-omic atlas of T cell exhaustion. These studies identified pathways regulated through transcriptional and post-translational mechanisms, including degradative and nondegradative ubiquitin modifications, and uncovered widespread changes in proteostasis, metabolism, and DNA repair. Major shifts were revealed in the ubiquitin-proteasome system, as differential expression of E3 ubiquitin ligases correlates with immunotherapy outcomes. These findings position the collapse of proteostasis as a central, underappreciated feature of T cell exhaustion and reveal opportunities to restore T cell function. We demonstrate that overexpression of the E3 ligase RNF166 enhances T cell persistence in vitro and in vivo. This work defines proteome-turnover dynamics as a critical regulatory layer in progressive T cell dysfunction, with broad implications for advancing cancer immunotherapy through manipulation of E3 ligases.

papers.title: A bioavailable GPX4 inhibitor for ferroptosis induction in vivo and tumor suppression.
papers.authors: Naowarojna N, Gu X, Pan Z, Yu J, Huang K, Zeng Y, Xie Y, Zhang Y, Wang F, Mao J, Yu Y, Wu TW, Yu J, Liu S, Xiao S, Bai L, Li D, Wu Z, Wei C, Li Q, Yao H, Zhang X, Li Y, Xie G, Gao L, Pan J, Wang L, Hu J, Feng X, Peng Q, Feng S, Wang X, Wang Y, Peng T, Wang Y, Zou Y.
papers.abstract: Ferroptosis is implicated in multiple human diseases, but the lack of bioavailable inducers has limited its physiological study and therapeutic translation. Here, we report KY0418, a selective covalent inhibitor of glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) featuring an isourea warhead, with high plasma stability and broad tissue distribution after oral dosing in mice. KY0418 specifically targets GPX4 SeCys46 to induce ferroptosis hallmarks in human and mouse cancer cell lines, with greater selectivity than existing inhibitors. In a standardizable acute-liver-injury mouse model, KY0418 triggers ferroptotic ultrastructural changes matching those of established inducers, and systemic administration remodels tissue metabolism and generates hydroxyl radicals detectable by a chemiluminescent probe. Subcutaneous tumors from different cancers exhibited variable responses to KY0418 treatment, from no effect to about 70% growth inhibition, but KY0418 consistently eradicated circulating tumor cells and suppressed metastasis across multiple cancer models. These findings position KY0418 as a tool for advancing in vivo ferroptosis research and its clinical translation.

papers.title: In vivo Gene Writing with engineered retrotransposons.
papers.authors: Li D, De Iaco A, Ngan KC, Smyshlyaev G, Kumbhojkar N, Steinberg BE, Kalani Z, Xia L, Dolbee A, Kibbler ES, Duncan MC, Lin I, Benczkowski MS, Venkatesan L, Calabria A, Carter TA, Corsi GI, Kristiansen TA, McAllister G, Bolt CC, Harris KA, Boucher JI, Zeng C, Dakhara IS, Wang X, Sothiselvam S, Akinci E, Strickland J, Mathur A, Ferren C, Desmond J, Rodriguez J, Rottman JB, Gupta M, Liu L, Palchaudhuri R, Wang ZJ, Citorik RJ, Rubens JR, Pujar NS, Holmes MC, Cotta-Ramusino C.
papers.abstract: Efficient integration of gene-length cargos in vivo remains challenging. Non-long terminal repeat (non-LTR) retrotransposons, which naturally mobilize large DNA segments through an RNA intermediate, could potentially address these limitations. Here, we developed a computational pipeline to systematically identify a diverse set of non-LTR retrotransposons. Extensive engineering generated elements capable of the efficient and stable insertion of reporter genes in human cells using RNA templates introduced in trans, which we term Gene Writers. Gene Writers successfully generated CD19 and CD20 chimeric antigen receptor T (CAR-T) cells ex vivo with robust antitumor activity. Lipid nanoparticle-mediated RNA delivery enabled in vivo CAR-T cell generation and stable B cell depletion in a humanized mouse model. Our study delineates a comprehensive framework for the discovery, engineering, and application of non-LTR retrotransposons and demonstrates their utility for gene-sized cargo delivery in vivo, thereby bridging a critical gap in existing gene therapy modalities.

papers.title: Type I IFN promotes ILC2-to-ILC1 plasticity in pre-clinical radiation-induced lung injury.
papers.authors: Kim J, Li H, Mannan R, Doherty TA, McGee HM.
papers.abstract: Radiation-induced lung injury (RILI) is a common dose-limiting toxicity after radiotherapy for lung cancer, but the immunological mechanisms contributing to RILI pathogenesis remain poorly understood. Here we analyze a RILI mouse model using high-dose, restricted-field irradiation to the left lung. Flow cytometry and cytokine profiling analysis of innate lymphoid cells (ILC) reveals a radiation-induced shift from lung-resident type 2 ILCs (ILC2) toward pro-inflammatory type 1 ILCs (ILC1). Single-cell RNA-sequencing analysis of mouse lung ILC populations after radiation suggests that type I interferon (IFN) promotes radiation-induced ILC2-to-ILC1 plasticity. In vitro, IFN-β stimulation of mouse ILC2s leads to increased expression of the ILC1 markers T-bet and IFN-γ, while IFN-β stimulation of human peripheral blood mononuclear cells increases the ILC1-to-ILC2 ratio. In vivo, inhibition of type I IFN signaling attenuates lung damage after irradiation in our RILI model. Thus, our findings indicate that radiation-induced type I IFN induces ILC2-to-ILC1 plasticity to contribute to RILI pathogenesis, and suggest that targeting type I IFN signaling may be a therapeutic strategy to mitigate radiation-induced lung injury.

papers.title: Epithelial NF-κB shapes protective Treg cell responses to restrain intestinal inflammation.
papers.authors: Barleben L, Schneegans AJ, Uyar B, Bruneau A, Vasileva G, Flohr F, Kabrani E, Vasilakis T, Hammann L, Gebert P, Dietrich C, Bochow-Fitzner B, Arnold A, Sai S, Gröne F, Sander M, Conrad T, Gérard A, Piseddu I, Anz D, Jochum C, Akalin A, Hammerich L, Klose CSN, Tacke F, Di Virgilio M, Kolesnichenko M.
papers.abstract: Inflammation resolution depends on coordinated communication between tissue compartments, yet how the intestinal epithelium shapes its immune microenvironment remains poorly understood. Here, using colonic biopsies from patients with ulcerative colitis (UC) and mouse models enabling tissue-wide visualization of NF-κB activity, we combine single-cell RNA sequencing and secretome analysis to define epithelial communication during colitis. We show that, paradoxically, the NF-κB-driven pro-inflammatory secretome of intestinal epithelial cells (IECs) is essential for recovery and prevents unrestrained inflammation. Mechanistically, epithelial NF-κB promotes CCL22-dependent regulatory T cell (Treg cell) recruitment and promotes a tolerogenic, pro-repair cell state, accompanied by induction of the lipid-metabolism-associated GDPD3 and CCR4. In UC, epithelial NF-κB is not uniformly activated but instead induces a selective pro-inflammatory transcriptional program while repressing targets regulating T cell recruitment. Thus, we identify dynamic epithelial-immune communication and demonstrate a protective IEC NF-κB-Treg cell axis important for resolution of intestinal inflammation.

papers.title: Blocking IL-6 trans-signaling mitigates benzalkonium chloride-induced inflammation, oxidative imbalance, ER stress, and barrier disruption in human corneal epithelial cells.
papers.authors: Lax K, Glass J, Aliste A, Sharma A, Sharma S.
papers.abstract: Background Benzalkonium chloride (BAC), a commonly used preservative in ophthalmic formulations, elicits a pro-inflammatory cytokine response and cytotoxic effects in corneal epithelial cells, contributing to ocular surface injuries associated with dry eye disease (DED). Interleukin-6 (IL-6) trans-signaling is a well-established pro-inflammatory pathway that contributes to endothelial and epithelial barrier dysfunction. Thus, this study investigated whether targeted inhibition of IL-6 trans-signaling with sgp130Fc could attenuate BAC-induced cytotoxic injury in corneal epithelial cells. Methods Human telomerase-immortalized corneal epithelial (hTCEpi) cells were exposed to 0.001% BAC for 30 min in the presence or absence of 10 μg/mL sgp130Fc. Markers of inflammation, oxidative imbalance, endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, and epithelial barrier disruption were assessed using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction, and western blot analyses. Reactive oxygen species (ROS), antioxidant capacity, and intracellular calcium flux were quantified using colorimetric, fluorescence-based, and luminescence-based assays. Epithelial barrier function was assessed using electric cell-substrate impedance sensing. Statistical analyses were performed using one-way analysis of variance followed by Tukey's or Holm-Šídák multiple-comparison tests, with P Results BAC exposure activated IL-6 trans-signaling as indicated by an increased sIL-6R/sgp130 ratio, reduced mIL-6R levels, and unchanged gp130 levels. BAC also increased secreted IL6 levels, IL6RA expression, and downstream inflammatory mediators MCP1 and ICAM1, all of which were attenuated by sgp130Fc. BAC-induced oxidative imbalance was characterized by increased ROS and hydrogen peroxide production, reduced antioxidant enzymes, and diminished total antioxidant capacity, whereas sgp130Fc mitigated these effects. In addition, BAC increased intracellular calcium levels and ER stress markers, including HSP72, BiP, PERK, and Ero1α, and impaired epithelial barrier function as observed by reduced trans-epithelial electrical resistance and decreased β-catenin, occludin, and claudin-1 levels. sgp130Fc mitigated increases in intracellular calcium, partially alleviated ER stress responses, and preserved epithelial barrier integrity and junctional protein levels. Conclusions These findings indicate that IL-6 trans-signaling contributes to BAC-induced corneal epithelial injury, suggesting that targeting this pathway may have therapeutic potential for DED and related ocular surface inflammatory disorders.

papers.title: A microbiome-bile acid axis mediates protection from chronic liver disease in females.
papers.authors: Li M, Kuang J, Chen T, Ding K, Chen Y, Jiao F, Li Y, Luo P, Xia L, Zhang H, Wang J, Zheng D, Zhao M, Sun T, Chao X, Guo Y, Zhu M, Sun Y, Xia X, Ge K, Qu C, Yao C, Xie G, Zhou K, Louca P, Menni C, Zhao A, Guo Q, Wan X, Zhang L, Ji G, Zhou J, Hu C, Jia W, Zheng X, Jia W.
papers.abstract: Sex-based differences in chronic liver disease (CLD) incidence and progression are well documented, yet the mechanistic basis of this sexual disparity remains elusive. Here, leveraging a large-scale metabolomics database comprising 9,254 individuals, we identify the endogenous bile acid, isoursodeoxycholic acid (isoUDCA), as a candidate mediator of female-associated hepatoprotection. We trace the origin of isoUDCA to a bacterial consortium, which is selectively enriched by estrogen through shaping a specialized intestinal microenvironment. Mechanistically, isoUDCA promotes the nuclear accumulation of SREBP2. This upregulates the intracellular transporter STARD4 and its functionally coupled downstream enzyme CYP7B1, thereby facilitating intracellular cholesterol handling and metabolic conversion. Collectively, our findings support a microbiome-bile acid-liver axis that may contribute to sex differences in CLD susceptibility and support further evaluation of isoUDCA as a potential therapeutic intervention.

papers.title: The pyrin inflammasome senses OCTN2-mediated uptake of extracellular ʟ-carnitine from muscle injury or ingestion.
papers.authors: Elliott EI, Yoshida TM, Nakandakari SCBR, Pope S, Zhang C, Nottoli T, Chae JJ, Kastner DL, Flavell RA, Dixit VD, Rathinam VA, Sutterwala FS, Wang A.
papers.abstract: Red-meat-containing diets are epidemiologically associated with diseases of chronic inflammation, while diets that restrict red meat improve health. Yet, it is uncertain how red meat incites inflammation. Here, we discover that ʟ-carnitine, an amino acid highly concentrated in skeletal muscle myocytes, drives inflammasome activation in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-challenged mice and LPS-primed murine and human macrophages. We find that extracellular ʟ-carnitine represses mevalonate synthesis, thereby triggering activation of the pyrin inflammasome, downstream of cellular import by the high-affinity ʟ-carnitine transporter OCTN2. We find that the inflammatory response to skeletal muscle injury also requires pyrin and OCTN2. Thus, in summary, we identify macrophages as sentinels of exogenous and endogenous extracellular ʟ-carnitine that serve as a proxy for skeletal myocyte damage, and we open the field to examine the mechanistic basis for how excess dietary intake of carnitine-rich food drives inflammatory disease.

papers.zh: 细胞病理学能否改善葡萄膜黑色素瘤 15-GEP/PRAME 预后预测？
papers.authors: Lane AM, Schefler AC, Correa ZM, et al.
papers.finding: 多中心队列研究评估在 15 基因表达谱与 PRAME 风险分层之外，确认性细胞病理结果是否影响葡萄膜黑色素瘤转移风险预测准确性。具体效应量需结合论文结果核对。
papers.why: 葡萄膜黑色素瘤的转移风险判定关系到随访密度、影像监测和患者咨询，是典型分子诊断临床转化问题。
papers.problem: 在已使用 GEP/PRAME 的条件下，传统细胞病理检查是否还能带来额外的预后价值。
papers.innovation: 结合多中心随访资料验证分子标志物与细胞病理学信息的互补性，直接针对临床工作流程。
papers.limitations: 当前演示仅核验研究目的与设计，未据全文分析具体效应值或最终结论，不能据此声称预后准确性提高。
papers.next: 核对原文完整统计结果后评估增量判别能力、校准度及决策曲线，并进行外部人群验证。

papers.title: Variables Associated With Faricimab Treatment Durability in Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration: A Post Hoc Analysis of the TENAYA and LUCERNE Trials
papers.zh: 哪些因素提示法瑞西单抗在新生血管性 AMD 中具有更长维持疗效？
papers.authors: Tan CS, Bakall B, Koh AHC, et al.
papers.finding: TENAYA/LUCERNE 试验事后分析发现，较低基线视网膜中央厚度和 PED 最大厚度，以及早期液体消退，与较长的法瑞西单抗给药间隔相关。
papers.why: 对高频就诊的 nAMD 患者而言，疗效持续时间直接影响注射负担、依从性和长期管理。
papers.problem: 如何在治疗早期识别更可能延长注射间隔的患者。
papers.innovation: 结合随机试验影像特征与早期解剖反应，寻找可能提示延长给药间隔的特征。
papers.limitations: 属于事后探索分析，部分 P 值未经多重比较校正；不能将相关性解释为稳定预测因子，且不能直接外推至其他药物。
papers.next: 前瞻性评估超过 16 周的个体化方案，并在真实世界研究中验证影像学预测模型。

papers.title: Comprehensive benchmarking of somatic mutation detection by the SMaHT Network
papers.zh: SMaHT 联盟系统评估体细胞突变检测技术与分析流程
papers.authors: Somatic Mosaicism across Human Tissues (SMaHT) Network
papers.finding: 联盟对短读长、长读长、双链及单细胞测序策略进行基准比较，显示供体特异性或泛基因组推断的二倍体组装可改善困难区域突变检出。
papers.why: 体细胞嵌合突变与衰老、癌症和非肿瘤性疾病相关，技术误差会直接影响临床与机制研究的可靠性。
papers.problem: 缺少统一、可复用的基准来比较不同测序与生信方案对低频体细胞突变的检出能力。
papers.innovation: 联合超深度短读长、长读长、六类双链测序及单细胞测序，强调跨技术互补并形成社区参考资源。
papers.limitations: 基准实验涉及九个分析样本；真实临床样本、低频变异和不同组织的表现仍需进一步外部验证。
papers.next: 在不同年龄、组织和疾病队列中开展独立复测，建立开放的跨平台基准流程并评估临床可迁移性。

papers.title: SpatialZoomer: multi-scale feature analysis of spatial transcriptomics
papers.zh: SpatialZoomer：空间转录组多尺度特征解析方法
papers.authors: Li X, Fan Y, Han Y, et al.
papers.abstract: A spectral graph-based spatial transcriptomics method uses low-pass filtering to extract molecular patterns at single-cell, niche and tissue-domain scales and identifies characteristic scales. Applied to Alzheimer disease progression and cancer microenvironments, it reports strong performance with relatively efficient computing.
papers.finding: 作者提出基于谱图低通滤波的 SpatialZoomer，在单细胞、细胞生态位和组织区域三个尺度提取空间分子特征，并在阿尔茨海默病和肿瘤微环境数据中展示了不同尺度的生物学信号。
papers.why: 单一空间尺度可能掩盖细胞间相互作用及组织结构。该方法强调空间尺度选择本身会改变识别到的细胞状态和疾病特征。
papers.problem: 空间转录组通常在固定分辨率下分析，难以系统比较不同组织尺度上的表达特征，也不易自动确定具有生物学意义的尺度。
papers.innovation: 将谱图滤波用于跨尺度特征提取，并通过跨尺度相似性图选择关键分辨率；论文同时讨论计算效率，并提供实现代码。
papers.limitations: 摘要与网页结果不足以完整判断在低测序深度、不同空间平台及复杂批次效应下的鲁棒性；关键性能差异、参数敏感性和外部验证仍需阅读全文及补充材料。
papers.next: 可进一步评估其在角膜新生血管、睑板腺或干眼眼表空间组学数据中的细胞生态位解析能力，并与细胞互作分析和病理空间标注联合验证。

papers.title: A microexon regulatory code reveals autism-linked genetic variation
papers.zh: 微外显子调控密码揭示与孤独症相关的遗传变异
papers.authors: Parada GE, Bretschneider H, et al.
papers.finding: 研究整合脑组织转录组及单核数据，扩展神经元微外显子图谱，并通过机器学习建立剪接调控序列模型，识别可能改变剪接的孤独症相关稀有变异。
papers.why: 将非编码调控变异与神经元特异性剪接连接，为解释部分既往难以定位功能的遗传风险提供新路径。
papers.problem: 微外显子注释不全，且难以系统预测非编码变异对神经元可变剪接的影响。
papers.innovation: 把大规模微外显子发现、神经元亚型差异与可解释的序列调控建模串联，形成可用于遗传变异优先级排序的框架。
papers.limitations: 变异影响多由模型预测和队列关联支持，不能直接等同于致病因果；细胞类型及功能实验仍需扩大验证。
papers.next: 结合患者来源 iPSC 神经元、长读长转录组及 CRISPR 碱基编辑，逐一验证候选变异对剪接和神经元表型的影响。

papers.title: Divergent genomic evolution in astrocytomas and oligodendrogliomas
papers.zh: 星形细胞瘤与少突胶质细胞瘤的基因组演化路径不同
papers.authors: Chowdhury T, Tesileanu CMS, et al.
papers.finding: 利用 GLASS 联盟 183 名 IDH 突变型胶质瘤患者纵向样本，发现星形细胞瘤更常累积拷贝数异常和染色体不稳定特征，而少突胶质细胞瘤倾向获得新驱动突变。
papers.why: 不同病理亚型的耐药及复发途径并不相同，或有助于设计个体化动态监测策略。
papers.problem: 胶质瘤如何在治疗与时间推移下发生遗传演化，以及不同亚型是否沿同一路径进展，仍存在缺口。
papers.innovation: 对同一患者多时间点全基因组/外显子组序列进行比较，分析不同肿瘤类型的演化差异。
papers.limitations: 队列以具备纵向手术标本的病例为主，存在样本选择与治疗异质性；分子轨迹不直接证明特定药物有效。
papers.next: 整合单细胞、空间组学和液体活检，追踪治疗压力下亚克隆的时间变化并验证预测性标志物。

papers.title: Computational design of metalloproteases
papers.zh: 利用计算蛋白设计构建可编程金属蛋白酶
papers.authors: Chen A, Wu K, Choi H, et al.
papers.finding: 使用 RFdiffusion 设计具有锌活性中心的蛋白酶；135 种设计中约 36% 可在目标位点切割肽链，并演示对 TDP-43、Aβ 等相关蛋白的选择性切割。
papers.why: 从蛋白结构生成跨越到高活性催化功能设计，是 AI 驱动分子工具研发的重要进展。
papers.problem: 从头设计能够高效、位点选择性切割稳定酰胺键的酶长期具有挑战。
papers.innovation: 联合结构生成、活性位点预组织优化与实验筛选；并以设计蛋白酶激活受控细胞因子，展示可编程生物调控。
papers.limitations: 主要处于生化和实验系统验证阶段，底物谱、脱靶切割、体内递送和免疫原性尚待系统评价。
papers.next: 扩展蛋白质组脱靶谱检测和体内功能评价，探索疾病靶向降解或局部激活型生物疗法。

papers.title: Mapping transcriptional responses to cellular perturbations with RNA fingerprinting
papers.zh: RNA 指纹将单细胞表达状态映射到扰动机制
papers.authors: Grabski IN, Lee J, Blair JD, et al.
papers.finding: 提出 RNA fingerprinting 方法，将新实验中的单细胞转录状态与遗传/化学扰动参考字典匹配，可解析 p53 调控、药物作用与感染相关免疫异质性。
papers.why: 单细胞描述性图谱非常丰富，而将未知细胞状态转化为可检验的扰动机制仍有明显缺口。
papers.problem: 如何把观察性单细胞数据与已有因果扰动实验连通，并进行概率化机制归因。
papers.innovation: 构建统计指纹表示并支持基因组规模、组合扰动与跨实验查询，形成可复用的机制检索方法。
papers.limitations: 表现依赖参考扰动字典覆盖范围；相关性匹配不自动等价于对新组织背景的因果证明。
papers.next: 结合空间转录组、CRISPR 验证及跨平台批次效应评估，建立更广泛的扰动参考图库。
